title.zh: 卷七十一 皇甫嵩朱儁列傳
title.en: Volume 71: Biographies of Huangfu Song, Zhu Jun
title.raw: 卷七十一 皇甫嵩朱儁列傳 Volume 71: Biographies of Huangfu Song, Zhu Jun

sentences.zh: 皇甫嵩

translations.literal: Huangfu Song.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Song.

sentences.zh: 皇甫嵩字義真，安定朝那人，度遼將軍規之兄子也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Song, courtesy name Yizhen, was a native of Chaona in Anding; he was the nephew of the General Who Crosses the Liao, Huangfu Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Song, styled Yizhen, came from Chaona in Anding Commandery and was nephew to General Who Crosses the Liao Huangfu Gui.

sentences.zh: 父節，鴈門太守。

translations.literal: His father was Huangfu Jie, who served as Administrator of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Huangfu Jie, had been Administrator of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 嵩少有文武志介，好詩書，習弓馬。

translations.literal: In youth Song showed both civil and martial resolve, loved the classics, and trained in archery and horsemanship.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he showed civil and martial ambition, loved letters, and drilled in bow and saddle.

sentences.zh: 初舉孝廉、茂才。

translations.literal: At first he was nominated Filial and Incorrupt and as Abundant Talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was first recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and as Abundant Talent.

sentences.zh: [1]太尉陳蕃、大將軍竇武連辟，並不到。

translations.literal: [1] Grand Commandant Chen Fan and General-in-Chief Dou Wu summoned him repeatedly; he did not go to either.
translations.idiomatic: [1] Grand Commandant Chen Fan and General-in-Chief Dou Wu repeatedly summoned him to office, yet he refused every appointment.

sentences.zh: 靈帝公車徵為議郎，遷北地太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling summoned him by imperial carriage to serve as Court Gentleman Consultant and promoted him to Administrator of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling called him to the capital as a Court Gentleman Consultant and later promoted him to Administrator of Beidi.

sentences.zh: 儁前與賊波才戰，戰敗，嵩因進保長社。

translations.literal: Earlier Jun had fought the rebel Bo Cai and been defeated, so Song advanced and held Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jun had already clashed with the rebel Bo Cai and lost; Song therefore moved up and secured Changshe.

sentences.zh: 波才引大衆圍城，嵩兵少，軍人皆恐，乃召軍吏謂曰：「兵有奇變，不在衆寡。

translations.literal: Bo Cai led a great host to surround the city. Song’s troops were few and his soldiers were all afraid, so he summoned his officers and said: ‘Warfare admits strange shifts; it does not lie in numbers alone.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Cai brought a huge force to invest the walls. Song was badly outnumbered and panic spread through the camp, until he gathered his officers and told them, ‘In war, surprise turns the scale—numbers alone do not decide it.’

sentences.zh: [7]今賊依草結營，易為風火。

translations.literal: [7] Now the enemy have camped among the grass; they are easily struck by wind and fire.
translations.idiomatic: [7] These men have pitched their camps in the dry grass—they are vulnerable to wind and fire.

sentences.zh: 若因夜縱燒，必大驚亂。

translations.literal: If we take advantage of the night to set them ablaze, they will surely panic and fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait for night and send flames through their lines, they will break in terror.

sentences.zh: 吾出兵擊之，四面俱合，田單之功可成也。

translations.literal: If we then sally forth and strike them, closing in on every side, the achievement of Tian Dan can be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Then we sortie from the gates and close every side—the feat Tian Dan once pulled off at Jimo can be ours.

sentences.zh: 」[8]其夕遂大風，嵩乃約勑軍士皆束苣乘城，[9]使銳士閒出圍外，縱火大呼，城上舉燎應之，嵩因鼓而奔其陳，賊驚亂奔走。

translations.literal: ’[8] That very evening a great wind sprang up. Song ordered his men to bind torches and man the walls; [9] he sent picked troops out through the siege by stealth, set fires, and raised a great shout. Signal fires blazed on the wall in answer; Song then beat the drums and charged their formation. The rebels panicked and fled.
translations.idiomatic: ’[8] That night the wind rose as if on cue. Song had every man bundle rushes and take position on the battlements; [9] elite squads slipped through the ring, lit the camps, and roared the alarm; bonfires flared along the wall in reply. Song crashed the drums and drove straight into their ranks. The Yellow Turbans scattered in chaos.

sentences.zh: 會帝遣騎都尉曹操將兵適至，嵩、操與朱儁合兵更戰，大破之，斬首數萬級。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor dispatched Cavalry Commandant Cao Cao with troops, who arrived opportunely; Song and Cao joined Zhu Jun and fought again, routing them utterly and taking tens of thousands of heads.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Cao Cao arrived at the head of an imperial column; Song and Cao united with Zhu Jun, renewed the battle, and shattered the defenders, claiming tens of thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 封嵩都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Song was enfeoffed as marquis of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The court invested Huangfu Song as Marquis of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 嵩、儁乘勝進討汝南、陳國黃巾，追波才於陽翟，擊彭脫於西華，並破之。

translations.literal: Song and Jun pressed their victory into Runan and the Yellow Turbans of Chen state, pursued Bo Cai to Yangdi, struck Peng Tuo at Xihua, and defeated both.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Zhu Jun carried the pursuit into Runan and Chen, ran Bo Cai down at Yangdi, crushed Peng Tuo at Xihua, and broke both bands.

sentences.zh: [10]餘賊降散，三郡悉平。

translations.literal: [10] The remaining rebels surrendered or scattered; all three commanderies were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: [10] The surviving rebels capitulated or melted away, and three commanderies were declared quiet.

sentences.zh: 又進擊東郡黃巾卜己於倉亭，生禽卜己，斬首七千餘級。

translations.literal: Next they advanced against the Yellow Turbans of Dong command under Bu Ji at Cangting, captured Bu Ji alive, and took more than seven thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed on to Cangting in Dong command, seized the Yellow Turban leader Bu Ji alive, and piled up over seven thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 時北中郎將盧植及東中郎將董卓討張角，並無功而還，乃詔嵩進兵討之。

translations.literal: At that time General of the Northern Army Lu Zhi and General of the Eastern Army Dong Zhuo had campaigned against Zhang Jiao without success and returned, so an edict ordered Song to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Army general Lu Zhi and Eastern Army general Dong Zhuo had failed against Zhang Jiao and withdrawn; the throne now commanded Song to take up the offensive.

sentences.zh: 嵩與角弟梁戰於廣宗。

translations.literal: Song fought Zhang Jiao’s younger brother Liang at Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Song met Zhang Liang—Zhang Jiao’s younger brother—near Guangzong.

sentences.zh: [11]梁衆精勇，嵩不能克。

translations.literal: [11] Liang’s host was picked and fierce; Song could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: [11] Liang’s veterans were fierce and fresh, and Song could not break them.

sentences.zh: 明日，乃閉營休士，以觀其變。

translations.literal: The next day he shut the camps and rested the troops to watch how conditions shifted.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he stood down, sealed the camps, and waited to see what the enemy would do.

sentences.zh: 知賊意稍懈，乃潛夜勒兵，雞鳴馳赴其陳，戰至晡時，大破之，斬梁，獲首三萬級，赴河死者五萬許人，焚燒車重三萬餘兩，悉虜其婦子，繫獲甚衆。

translations.literal: Perceiving that the rebels were slackening, he secretly marshalled his army by night, rode at cockcrow straight into their lines, and fought until late afternoon, routing them utterly. Liang was beheaded; thirty thousand heads were taken; some fifty thousand drowned trying to cross the river; more than thirty thousand wagons were burned; women and children were seized wholesale and captives taken beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Once he sensed their guard slipping, he moved under cover of darkness, hit their camp at cockcrow, and hammered them until dusk. Liang fell; thirty thousand heads were counted; perhaps fifty thousand drowned in the river; thirty thousand supply carts went up in smoke; dependents were rounded up and prisoners numbered beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 角先已病死，乃剖棺戮屍，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiao had already died of illness; they opened his coffin, exposed the corpse to shame, and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiao had died of sickness weeks before; Song’s men exhumed him, dishonored the corpse, and forwarded the head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 嵩復與鉅鹿太守馮翊郭典攻角弟寶於下曲陽，又斬之。

translations.literal: Song again joined Giant Deer Administrator Guo Dian of Fengyi to strike Zhang Jiao’s younger brother Bao at Xiaquyang and beheaded him as well.
translations.idiomatic: With Giant Deer prefect Guo Dian of Fengyi he struck Zhang Bao at Xiaquyang and struck off his head too.

sentences.zh: 首獲十餘萬人，築京觀於城南。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand heads and captives were taken, and a burial mound of skulls was raised south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: They harvested upwards of a hundred thousand heads and prisoners and raised a victory mound of skulls south of the walls.

sentences.zh: [12]即拜嵩為左車騎將車，領冀州牧，封槐里侯，食槐里、美陽兩縣，[13]合八千戶。

translations.literal: [12] Song was immediately appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry on the Left—note that the received text writes ‘general of chariots’—Governor of Ji province, enfeoffed as marquis of Huaili with income from Huaili and Meiyang counties, [13] eight thousand households in all.
translations.idiomatic: [12] He was named General of Chariots and Cavalry on the Left (the transmitted graph ‘chariot’ is likely a scribal slip for ‘general’), Governor of Ji, Marquis of Huaili with two counties as his fief, [13] totaling eight thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以黃巾既平，故改年為中平。

translations.literal: Because the Yellow Turbans had been crushed, the reign title was changed to Zhongping.
translations.idiomatic: With the rebellion crushed, the court adopted the new era name Zhongping.

sentences.zh: 嵩奏請冀州一年田租，以贍饑民，帝從之。

translations.literal: Song memorialized to remit one year of land tax in Ji to relieve the starving; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Song asked that Ji province’s grain levy be waived for a year to feed the hungry, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 百姓歌曰：「天下大亂兮市為墟，母不保子兮妻失夫，賴得皇甫兮復安居。

translations.literal: The common people sang: ‘The realm is in chaos and the marketplaces lie in ruins; mothers cannot keep their sons nor wives their husbands—thanks to Huangfu we dwell in peace again.
translations.idiomatic: Folk sang: ‘Heaven’s disorder turns bazaars to wasteland; mothers lose sons and wives lose husbands—yet Huangfu gave us back a roof and a hearth.’

sentences.zh: 」嵩溫恤士卒，甚得衆情，每軍行頓止，須營幔修立，然後就舍帳。

translations.literal: ’ Song treated his soldiers with kindness and won deep affection; whenever the army halted he waited until the camp curtains were set up before entering his own tent.
translations.idiomatic: ’ Song warmed to his men and they loved him in return: at every halt he would not retire until the camp stood ready—only then did he take his own quarters.

sentences.zh: 軍士皆食，*

translations.literal: Not until every soldier had finished eating
translations.idiomatic: Not until every soldier had eaten

translations.literal: did Song
translations.idiomatic: would Huangfu Song

sentences.zh: **[己]*乃嚐飯。

translations.literal: only then taste his own meal.
translations.idiomatic: sit down to his own meal.

sentences.zh: 吏有因事受賂者，嵩更以錢物賜之，吏懷籩，或至自殺。

translations.literal: When minor officials accepted bribes on some pretext, Song gave them money and goods instead; ashamed beyond bearing, some killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If an aide took a bribe, Song pressed silver and goods on him until shame overcame the man—some went so far as suicide.

sentences.zh: 嵩既破黃巾，威震天下，而朝政日亂，海內虛困。

translations.literal: Once Song had shattered the Yellow Turbans his prestige shook the realm, yet court government grew worse by the day and the empire hollowed with exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: After the Turbans fell, Song’s name terrified every quarter, but Luoyang slid deeper into disorder and the country starved.

sentences.zh: 故信都令漢陽閻忠干說嵩曰：

translations.literal: Therefore Yan Zhong, former magistrate of Xindu from Hanyang, presumptuously urged Song:
translations.idiomatic: So Yan Zhong of Hanyang, who had been magistrate of Xindu, waylaid Song with a dangerous proposition:

sentences.zh: [14]「難得而易失者，時也；

translations.literal: [14] ‘What is hard to win and easy to lose is the hour;
translations.idiomatic: [14] ‘The moment that cannot be grasped twice is occasion;

sentences.zh: 時至不旋踵者，幾也。

translations.literal: what comes at its hour yet allows no heel-turn is opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: the instant that brooks no delay is chance.’

sentences.zh: 故聖人順時以動，智者因幾以發。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage moves with the times; the wise man strikes when opportunity appears.
translations.idiomatic: The sage rides the tide; the keen eye strikes when fate opens a crack.’

sentences.zh: 今將軍遭難得之運，蹈易駭之機，而踐運不撫，臨機不發，將何以保大名乎？

translations.literal: Now you, General, have met a fortune rarely granted and tread upon an opening that easily alarms others; yet having stepped into fortune you do not seize it, and facing opportunity you do not act—how will you preserve your great name?
translations.idiomatic: ‘You stand on a blessing few receive and a hinge-point that would frighten lesser men—and still you refuse to embrace the one or strike the other. How long can glory like yours survive?’

sentences.zh: 」嵩曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: ’ Song said: ‘What do you mean?
translations.idiomatic: Song answered, ‘Explain yourself.’

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「天道無親，百姓與能。

translations.literal: ’ Zhong said: ‘Heaven’s way shows no partiality; the common people invest their hopes in whoever proves worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong continued: ‘Heaven is impartial—the crowd backs whoever shows strength.

sentences.zh: 今將軍受鉞於暮春，收功於末冬。

translations.literal: Now you received the battle-axe in late spring and harvested victory by winter’s end.
translations.idiomatic: You took the axe in spring’s last month and sealed success before winter closed.’

sentences.zh: [15]兵動若神，謀不再計，摧強易於折枯，消堅甚於湯雪，旬月之閒，神兵電埽，封屍刻石，南向以報，威德震本朝，風聲馳海外，雖湯武之舉，未有高將軍者也。

translations.literal: [15] Your armies move like spirits; you plot once and need not plot twice; breaking the strong is easier than snapping dry wood; melting the hardened is swifter than boiling snow. Within the span of a month divine soldiers swept like lightning; corpses were piled and stone monuments carved; reports went south to the throne; awe and virtue shook the capital and your fame raced beyond the seas—not even the deeds of Tang or Wu tower above yours.
translations.idiomatic: [15] Your hosts strike like gods; one calculation suffices where others need many; strong lines crumble like deadwood and hardened foes melt like frost in sun. In mere weeks your men scoured the plain like lightning, raised victory mounds, and carried word south—the court trembled at your virtue and rumor crossed the seas. Tang and Wu themselves did no more.’

sentences.zh: 今身建不賞之功，體兼高人之德，而北面庸主，何以求安乎？

translations.literal: Now you embody merit beyond any reward and bear the virtue of a towering man, yet you bow north to a mediocre lord—how can you hope for safety?
translations.idiomatic: ‘Yet you kneel to a feckless sovereign with achievements no medal can repay and a character fit for the ages—where is safety in that?’

sentences.zh: 」嵩曰：「夙夜在公，心不忘忠，何故不安？」

translations.literal: ’ Song said: ‘Night and day I labor for the state; my heart never forgets loyalty—why should I not be secure?
translations.idiomatic: Song replied, ‘I serve the common weal day and night; disloyalty is far from my mind—why should I fear?’

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「不然。

translations.literal: ’ Zhong said: ‘It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: ‘That is not how power works,’ said Zhong.

sentences.zh: 昔韓信不忍一餐之遇，而棄三分之業，利劒已揣其喉，方發悔毒之歎者，機失而謀乖也。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Xin could not bear to cast aside a single meal’s kindness and so threw away the enterprise of three parts; the keen sword was already at his throat before he uttered his bitter regrets—because the moment had slipped and his plans went awry.
translations.idiomatic: Think of Han Xin: he clung to one kind meal and forfeited a tripartite empire; steel was already at his throat before he groaned with regret—timing failed and strategy soured.’

sentences.zh: [16]今主上埶弱於劉、項，將軍權重於淮陰，指撝足以振風雲，叱宛可以興雷電。

translations.literal: [16] Today our sovereign is feebler than Liu Bang or Xiang Yu; your authority outweighs the lord of Huaiyin—a gesture of your hand can stir wind and cloud; a shout can conjure thunder and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: [16] Your emperor is weaker than Liu Bang or Xiang Yu ever were, while your grip exceeds Han Xin’s—a wave of your arm stirs storm; a shout could pass for thunder.’

sentences.zh: [17]赫然奮發，因危扺頹，[18]崇恩以綏先附，振武以臨後服，徵冀方之士，動七州之衆，羽檄先馳於前，大軍響振於後，蹈流漳河，飲馬孟津，誅閹官之罪，除腢凶之積，雖僮兒可使奮拳以致力，女子可使褰裳以用命，況厲熊羆之卒，因迅風之埶哉！

translations.literal: [17] Rise in wrath and exploit crisis to topple what totters; [18] heap kindness on those who yield first and brandish force against those who lag; summon worthy men from Ji, set the hosts of seven provinces in motion; dispatch feathered dispatches ahead and let the great army thunder behind—ford the Zhang’s current and water horses at Mengjin; execute the guilt of the palace eunuchs and scour away accumulated villainy. Even boys could clench fists to serve you and women could tuck up skirts to obey—how much more your fierce veterans riding the gale!
translations.idiomatic: [17] Shake off restraint, ride collapse when it comes; [18] shower favor on early allies and shock the hesitant with arms; rally Ji’s talent, march the levies of seven provinces; let urgent orders fly before you and the main host boom behind—cross the Zhang, water at Mengjin, put the eunuchs to the sword, and rinse away piled-up corruption. Children would strike for you and women march—need one speak of tiger troops borne on a hurricane?’

sentences.zh: 功業已就，天下已順，然後請呼上帝，示以天命，混齊六合，南面稱制，移寶器於將興，[19]推亡漢於已墜，實神機之至會，風發之良時也。

translations.literal: When the achievement stands complete and All Under Heaven already bows, then invoke High Heaven, proclaim the Mandate, unite the six directions, face south as sovereign, shift the sacred tripods to the rising house, [19] and topple the dying Han while it still falls—such is the supreme conjunction of divine strategy and the favorable hour when the wind is at your back.
translations.idiomatic: Finish the work, win the realm’s assent, call upon Heaven, display the Mandate, weld the quarters under one throne, move the bronze tripods toward the dynasty-to-be, [19] and tip the moribund Han off the cliff—that is destiny’s rare nod and the gale at your stern.’

sentences.zh: 夫既朽不雕，衰世難佐。

translations.literal: Timber already rotten cannot be carved; a declining age is hard to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Rotten timber will not take the chisel; a dying age defies counsel.’

sentences.zh: 若欲輔難佐之朝，雕朽敗之木，是猶逆坂走丸，迎風縱棹，豈云易哉？

translations.literal: If you wish to prop up a court beyond aiding and carve wood already spoiled, it is like rolling a ball uphill or rowing straight into the wind—can anyone call that easy?
translations.idiomatic: Try to shore up such a throne or plane such timber and you roll a stone up a slope or beat upstream—nothing easy lives there.’

sentences.zh: 且今豎宦腢居，同惡如市，[20]上命不行，權歸近習，昏主之下，難以久居，[21]不賞之功，讒人側目，如不早圖，後悔無及。

translations.literal: Moreover eunuchs swarm like goods in a market [20]; imperial commands do not run and power rests with favorites; under a benighted lord one cannot long endure; [21] merit beyond reward draws envious glares—if you do not plan early, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the castrates pack the palace like hawkers [20]; edicts die on the steps while intimates hold the seal; no loyal minister lasts under a dim king; [21] rewards cannot match your fame and slanderers already slant their eyes—wait, and remorse arrives bare-handed.’

sentences.zh: 」嵩懼曰：「非常之謀，不施於有常之埶。

translations.literal: Song said in alarm: ‘Extraordinary schemes are not applied to ordinary circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Song said, shaken, ‘Plots fit for upheaval do not suit ordinary times.

sentences.zh: 創圖大功，豈庸才所致。

translations.literal: Founding a grand achievement out of nothing—is that something a mediocre talent can accomplish?
translations.idiomatic: Building an empire from nothing is no job for small gifts.’

sentences.zh: 黃巾細孽，敵非秦、項，新結易散，難以濟業。

translations.literal: The Yellow Turbans were petty evil; the foe was no Qin or Xiang Yu; newly gathered bands scatter easily and cannot sustain a great undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: ‘The Turbans were rabble, not Qin or Chu; such rabble breaks up faster than it builds.’

sentences.zh: 且人未忘主，天不佑逆。

translations.literal: Moreover the people have not forgotten their ruler; Heaven does not bless rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The people still honor their emperor; Heaven backs no traitor.’

sentences.zh: 若虛造不冀之功，以速朝夕之禍，孰與委忠本朝，守其臣節。

translations.literal: If I invent merit that cannot be hoped for and hasten disaster within days, how does that compare with committing loyalty to this court and preserving a minister’s integrity?
translations.idiomatic: ‘To chase phantom glory and court swift ruin—how does that stack against steadfast service and intact honor?’

sentences.zh: 雖云多讒，不過放廢，猶有令名，死且不朽。

translations.literal: Though slander may abound, at worst I would be dismissed and cast aside; I would still keep a fair name and die without decay.
translations.idiomatic: Even envoys of spite can only strip my office; my name stays clean and death cannot stain it.’

sentences.zh: [22]反常之論，所不敢聞。

translations.literal: [22] Counsel that overturns the norm I dare not hear.
translations.idiomatic: [22] I will not hear plots against the grain.’

sentences.zh: 」忠知計不用，因亡去。

translations.literal: ’ Zhong knew his plan would not be adopted and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong saw he had lost Song and vanished.

translations.literal: Editorial commentary marker [23] stands here in the transmitted text.
translations.idiomatic: The received edition carries an annotator’s tag for note twenty-three at this point.

sentences.zh: 會邊章、韓遂作亂隴右，明年春，詔嵩回鎮長安，以衛園陵。

translations.literal: As it happened, Bian Zhang and Han Sui rebelled in Longyou; the next spring an edict ordered Song back to garrison Chang’an to guard the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian Zhang and Han Sui rose on the Long right, an edict the following spring sent Song back to hold Chang’an and shield the mausolea.

sentences.zh: 章等遂復入寇三輔，使嵩因討之。

translations.literal: Zhang and his fellows then raided the Three Adjuncts again, and the court had Song strike them on that account.
translations.idiomatic: They poured into the Three Adjuncts once more, and Song was told to take them in hand.

sentences.zh: 初，嵩討張角，路由鄴，見中常侍趙忠舍宅踰制，乃奏沒入之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Song campaigned against Zhang Jiao, his route passed Ye; seeing that Grand Coachman Zhao Zhong’s mansion exceeded statutory scale, he memorialized to confiscate it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhang Jiao campaign his road ran through Ye; finding Attendant Zhao Zhong’s compound outrageously grand, he seized it by memorial.

sentences.zh: 又中常侍張讓私求錢五千萬，嵩不與，二人由此為憾，奏嵩連戰無功，所費者多。

translations.literal: Grand Coachman Zhang Rang privately demanded fifty million cash; Song refused. The two nursed a grudge and memorialized that Song had fought repeatedly without success at great expense.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Zhang Rang privately demanded fifty million cash and was refused; both men bore a grudge and accused Song of wasting treasure on fruitless battles.

sentences.zh: 其秋徵還，收左車騎將軍印綬，削戶六千，更封都鄉侯，二千戶。

translations.literal: That autumn he was recalled, stripped of the seal ribbon of General of Chariots and Cavalry on the Left, reduced by six thousand households, re-enfeoffed as marquis of Duxiang at two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn they recalled him, lifted his credentials as General of Chariots and Cavalry on the Left, carved six thousand households from his fief, and reissued him as Marquis of Duxiang at two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 五年，*

translations.literal: In the fifth year,
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhongping,

translations.literal: (The manuscript fragment reads a graph homophonous with ‘Liang’; critical editions emend to Liangzhou.)
translations.idiomatic: (Scribal slip: the name should be Liangzhou, not the unrelated Liang.)

sentences.zh: **[涼]*州賊王國圍陳倉，復拜嵩為左將軍，督前將軍董卓，各率二萬人拒之。

translations.literal: **[Liang]**zhou rebel Wang Guo besieged Chen Cang; Song was again appointed General of the Left and directed Former General Dong Zhuo; each led twenty thousand men to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Liangzhou under Wang Guo invested Chen Cang; Song was restored as General of the Left with Dong Zhuo as Forward General—each commanded twenty thousand to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 卓欲速進赴陳倉，嵩不聽。

translations.literal: Zhuo wished to hurry forward to Chen Cang; Song would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo pressed for a forced march to lift the siege; Song refused.

sentences.zh: 卓曰：「智者不後時，勇者不留決。

translations.literal: Zhuo said: ‘The wise do not lag behind the hour; the brave do not postpone resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo argued, ‘The keen do not miss the moment; the bold do not defer the stroke.’

sentences.zh: 速救則城全，不救則城滅，全滅之埶，在於此也。

translations.literal: If we rescue swiftly the city survives; if we do not the city perishes—the outcome of survival or ruin hangs on this.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Swift relief preserves Chen Cang; delay destroys it—the pivot is now.’

sentences.zh: 」嵩曰：「不然。

translations.literal: ’ Song said: ‘It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Song answered, ‘Wrong.’

sentences.zh: 百戰百勝，不如不戰而屈人之兵。

translations.literal: To win a hundred battles a hundred times is not so good as defeating the enemy’s army without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: ‘A hundred victories in a hundred fights fall short of breaking the foe without crossing blades.’

sentences.zh: 是以先為不可勝，以待敵之可勝。

translations.literal: Therefore first make yourself unconquerable and await the enemy’s vulnerability.
translations.idiomatic: First become unassailable, then wait until they expose a flaw.’

sentences.zh: 不可勝在我，可勝在彼。

translations.literal: Being unconquerable lies with me; being vulnerable lies with them.
translations.idiomatic: Defense is ours to master; vulnerability is theirs to grant.’

sentences.zh: 彼守不足，我攻有餘。

translations.literal: Their defense is inadequate while our attack has surplus.
translations.idiomatic: They defend from weakness; we attack from strength.’

sentences.zh: [24]有餘者動於九天之上，不足者陷於九地之下。

translations.literal: [24] Where there is surplus, movement is as if above the ninth heaven; where there is inadequacy, one sinks into the ninth layer of earth.
translations.idiomatic: [24] Strength strikes from the ninth heaven; weakness sinks to the ninth abyss.’

sentences.zh: [25]今陳倉雖小，城守固備，非九地之陷也。

translations.literal: [25] Chen Cang is small, yet its walls and preparations are firm—it is no abyss into which guard troops sink.
translations.idiomatic: [25] Chen Cang is tiny but its ramparts are tight—not the ‘ninth abyss’ of doomed defense.’

sentences.zh: 王國雖強，而攻我之所不救，非九天之埶也。

translations.literal: Though Wang Guo is strong, he attacks where we choose not to rescue; it is not the posture of one who moves above the ninth heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo may be fierce, yet he spends his fury on a city we need not rescue—hardly the stance of strength raining blows from on high.’

sentences.zh: 夫埶非九天，攻者受害；

translations.literal: When posture is not above the ninth heaven, the attacker suffers harm;
translations.idiomatic: Without that height the attacker bleeds;

sentences.zh: 陷非九地，守者不拔。

translations.literal: when sinking is not into the ninth earth, the defenders cannot be uprooted.
translations.idiomatic: without that depth the garrison never yields.’

sentences.zh: 國今已陷受害之地，而陳倉保不拔之城，我可不煩兵動衆，而取全勝之功，將何救焉！

translations.literal: Guo now stands on ground where attackers suffer harm, while Chen Cang holds an unyielding city—why should we weary hosts of troops when complete victory can be taken without battle? What need is there to rush a rescue?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo has stumbled onto ground that consumes attackers, while Chen Cang remains an iron nut—why exhaust our legions when patience buys total victory? What use is a reckless relief?’

sentences.zh: 」遂不聽。

translations.literal: ’ He therefore refused.
translations.idiomatic: Song held his ground.

sentences.zh: 王國圍陳倉，自冬迄春，八十餘日，城堅守固，竟不能拔。

translations.literal: Wang Guo besieged Chen Cang from winter through spring for more than eighty days; the walls stood firm and he could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: For eighty days from winter into spring Wang Guo battered Chen Cang and gained no breach.

sentences.zh: 賊衆疲敝，果自解去。

translations.literal: The rebel host wore out and indeed lifted the siege of its own accord.
translations.idiomatic: His army frayed and slipped away of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 嵩進兵擊之。

translations.literal: Song advanced his troops and attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: Song marched after them.

sentences.zh: 卓曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Zhuo said: ‘We cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo warned, ‘Stop.’

sentences.zh: 兵法，窮寇勿*

translations.literal: According to military doctrine, do not press a cornered foe—
translations.idiomatic: The canon says: Never harry a foe driven desperate—

translations.literal: (press)
translations.idiomatic: (The variant reading is ‘press, harry’.)

translations.literal: —nor press a retreating host—
translations.idiomatic: —nor chase a retreating mass—

translations.literal: (pursue)
translations.idiomatic: (The alternate reading is ‘pursue’.)

translations.literal: —with further pressure.
translations.idiomatic: —with another surge.’

sentences.zh: [26]今我追國，是迫歸衆，追窮寇也。

translations.literal: [26] If we pursue Guo now we press a retreating mass and drive cornered bandits.
translations.idiomatic: [26] Pursuing Wang Guo means harassing a withdrawal and hunting men with nothing left to lose.’

sentences.zh: 困獸猶鬭，蜂蠆有毒，[27]況大衆乎！」

translations.literal: A cornered beast still fights; hornets and scorpions carry venom—[27] how much more a great multitude!
translations.idiomatic: ‘Even a beast at bay turns; bees and scorpions sting—[27] what of an army?’

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「不然。

translations.literal: ’ Song said: ‘It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Song said, ‘No.’

sentences.zh: 前吾不擊，避其銳也。

translations.literal: Earlier I did not strike because I avoided their keen edge.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Before, I held back to blunt their edge.’

sentences.zh: 今而擊之，待其衰也。

translations.literal: Now we strike them because we wait until they decline.
translations.idiomatic: We strike now precisely because we let their strength run down.

sentences.zh: 所擊疲師，非歸衆也。

translations.literal: Those we strike are exhausted troops, not a mass on an orderly withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Our target is a worn-out army, not men marching home in good order.

sentences.zh: 國衆且走，莫有鬭志。

translations.literal: Guo’s host is already fleeing; none retains the will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo’s men are on the run and have lost the stomach for battle.

sentences.zh: 以整擊亂，非窮寇也。

translations.literal: With order attacking disorder, they are not cornered desperadoes.
translations.idiomatic: We hit chaos with discipline—these are not foe driven to the last ditch.

sentences.zh: 」遂獨進擊之，使卓為後拒。

translations.literal: ’ He therefore advanced alone to attack them and ordered Zhuo to cover the rear.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the pursuit alone and told Dong Zhuo to hold the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 連戰大破之，斬首萬餘級，國走而死。

translations.literal: Battle after battle he shattered them, taking more than ten thousand heads; Guo fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: He routed them repeatedly, piled up over ten thousand heads, and Wang Guo bolted only to perish on the road.

sentences.zh: 卓大籩恨，由是忌嵩。

translations.literal: Zhuo nursed deep shame and resentment; from this he bore malice toward Song.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo burned with humiliation and jealousy and never forgave Song.

sentences.zh: 明年，卓拜為并州牧，詔使以兵委嵩，卓不從。

translations.literal: The next year Zhuo was appointed Governor of Bing province; an edict ordered him to hand his troops to Song, but Zhuo refused.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhuo became Governor of Bing; the court told him to yield command to Song, and he defied the order.

sentences.zh: 嵩從子酈[28]時在軍中，說嵩曰：「本朝失政，天下倒懸，能安危定傾者，唯大人與董卓耳。

translations.literal: Song’s nephew Li [28], then with the army, urged Song: ‘Our dynasty has lost the reins and the realm hangs upside down; only you, sir, and Dong Zhuo can steady the tipping vessel.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Li—note [28]—was in camp and warned him: ‘Han rule has slipped; only you and Dong Zhuo can set the tottering state upright.’

sentences.zh: 今怨隙已結，埶不俱存。

translations.literal: Now ill will is already tangled; the two of you cannot both endure.
translations.idiomatic: You have crossed blades in spirit; two such powers cannot share one sky.’

sentences.zh: 卓被詔委兵，而上書自請，此逆命也。

translations.literal: Zhuo received an edict to surrender his army yet memorialized to keep it—that is defiance of orders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was told to disband yet petitioned to stay armed—that is open insubordination.’

sentences.zh: 又以京師昏亂，躊躇不進，此懷奸也。

translations.literal: Again, because the capital is dark with turmoil he hesitates to advance—this is harboring treachery.
translations.idiomatic: He dawdles outside while Luoyang roils—that is treason dressed as caution.’

sentences.zh: 且其凶戾無親，將士不附。

translations.literal: Moreover he is brutal and trusts no kin; officers and men do not cleave to him.
translations.idiomatic: He is savage and faithless; his own troops barely tolerate him.’

sentences.zh: 大人今為元帥，杖國威以討之，上顯忠義，下除凶害，此桓文之事也。

translations.literal: You now command as supreme marshal; leaning on the state’s majesty to punish him, you display loyalty above and scourge a villain below—the deed of a Huan or a Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Take the baton as commander-in-chief, invoke imperial dignity against him, show loyalty to the throne and rid the realm of a brute—that is work worthy of Duke Huan or Duke Wen.’

sentences.zh: 」嵩曰：「專命雖罪，專誅亦有責也。

translations.literal: ’ Song said: ‘Though acting on one’s own authority is a crime, arbitrary execution also carries blame.
translations.idiomatic: Song answered: ‘To exceed orders is wrong; to kill a fellow minister without warrant is also blameful.’

sentences.zh: [29]不如顯奏其事，使朝廷裁之。

translations.literal: [29] Better to memorialize the facts plainly and let the court decide.
translations.idiomatic: [29] Better lay the evidence before the throne and let Luoyang judge.’

sentences.zh: 」於是上書以聞。

translations.literal: ’ He therefore submitted a memorial reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent up a full report.

sentences.zh: 帝讓卓，卓又增怨於嵩。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Zhuo, and Zhuo’s hatred toward Song deepened again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor scolded Zhuo, who hated Song all the more.

sentences.zh: 及後秉政，初平元年，乃徵嵩為城門校尉，因欲殺之。

translations.literal: Later, when Zhuo seized power, in the first year of Chuping he summoned Song as Colonel of the City Gates intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhuo held the government, in Chuping 1 he recalled Song as Colonel of the City Gates, meaning to murder him.

sentences.zh: 嵩將行，長史梁衍說曰：「漢室微弱，閹豎亂朝，董卓雖誅之，而不能盡忠於國，遂復寇掠京邑，廢立從意。

translations.literal: As Song was about to depart, Chief Clerk Liang Yan urged him: ‘The house of Han is feeble; castrates threw court into chaos; though Zhuo slew them he did not devote loyalty to the state—instead he plundered the capital at will and deposed or enthroned as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Song prepared to obey the summons; his chief clerk Liang Yan said: ‘Han withers; eunuchs ruined government; Zhuo cut them down yet serves only himself—looting Luoyang and swapping emperors like chess pieces.’

sentences.zh: 今徵將軍，大則危禍，小則困辱。

translations.literal: Now if you answer the summons, at worst you court calamity, at best humiliation and bondage.
translations.idiomatic: Go to Luoyang and you risk ruin at best disgrace.’

sentences.zh: 今卓在洛陽，天子來西，以將軍之衆，精兵三萬，迎接至尊，奉令討逆，發命海內，徵兵腢帥，袁氏逼其東，將軍迫其西，此成禽也。

translations.literal: Zhuo is in Luoyang while the Son of Heaven comes west; with your host—thirty thousand picked troops—you can welcome the supreme ruler, issue righteous orders to crush the rebel, call up commanders within the seas: the Yuans press him from the east, you from the west—he can be caged like a bird.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo holds the east; the emperor flees west—meet him with thirty thousand veterans, proclaim a loyal crusade, rally every warlord: Yuan’s coalition pins Zhuo from the east, you from the west, and he is finished.’

sentences.zh: 」嵩不從，遂就徵。

translations.literal: ’ Song would not listen and therefore obeyed the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Song declined the gamble and went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 有司承旨，奏嵩下吏，將遂誅之。

translations.literal: Officials, carrying out Zhuo’s intent, memorialized to commit Song to judicial custody and were about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers acting on Zhuo’s nod had Song thrown in jail and readied the headsman.

sentences.zh: 嵩子堅壽與卓素善，自長安亡走洛陽，歸投於卓。

translations.literal: Song’s son Jianshou, who had long been on good terms with Zhuo, fled from Chang’an to Luoyang and threw himself on Zhuo’s mercy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jianshou, once friendly with Zhuo, escaped Chang’an for Luoyang and pleaded for his father’s life.

sentences.zh: 卓方置酒歡會，堅壽直前質讓，責以大義，[30]叩頭流涕。

translations.literal: Zhuo was hosting a wine banquet in high spirits when Jianshou stepped forward, rebuked him face to face on the great principles, [30] and knocked his head to the ground weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was mid-feast when Jianshou strode in, upbraided him on honor and duty, [30] and battered his brow on the flags until blood mixed with tears.

sentences.zh: 坐者感動，皆離席請之。

translations.literal: Those seated were moved; all rose from their mats to intercede.
translations.idiomatic: Guests rose from their cushions, voices tangled in Song’s favor.

sentences.zh: 卓乃起，牽與共坐。

translations.literal: Zhuo then stood, took him by the hand, and seated him beside himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo relented, pulled the youth to his own bench, and shared his cup.

sentences.zh: 使免嵩囚，復拜嵩議郎，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He ordered Song released from prison, reappointed him Court Gentleman Consultant, and promoted him to Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He freed Song, restored him as Court Gentleman Consultant, and raised him to Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.

sentences.zh: 及卓還長安，公卿百官迎謁道次。

translations.literal: When Zhuo returned to Chang’an, dukes, ministers, and the hundred officials greeted him along the road.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhuo’s return to Chang’an the whole bureaucracy lined the highway to kowtow.

sentences.zh: 卓風令御史中丞已下皆拜以屈嵩，[31]既而扺手言曰：「義真犕未乎？

translations.literal: Zhuo hinted that everyone from the Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk downward should bow to humble Song; [31] then he clapped his hands and said: ‘Yizhen, are you still pulling the traces (unsubmissive)?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo compelled every clerk from Palace Assistant down to bow—and humiliate—Song; [31] then he sneered, ‘Yizhen, have you learned to wear the harness yet?’

sentences.zh: 」[32]嵩笑而謝之，卓乃解釋。

translations.literal: ’[32] Song smiled and apologized; Zhuo then relented.
translations.idiomatic: ’[32] Song forced a smile and mollified him; Zhuo’s temper cooled.

translations.literal: [33] Editorial commentary stands here in the transmitted text.
translations.idiomatic: [33] The manuscript preserves an editor’s tag at this juncture.

sentences.zh: 及卓被誅，以嵩為征西將軍，又遷車騎將軍。

translations.literal: After Zhuo was executed, Song was appointed General Who Conquers the West and later promoted General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuo fell, Song became General Who Conquers the West, then General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，拜太尉，冬，以流星策免。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed Grand Commandant; in winter he was dismissed on account of a shooting-star omen.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn brought him the Grand Commandancy; winter brought a comet and summary dismissal.

sentences.zh: [34]復拜光祿大夫，遷太常。

translations.literal: [34] He was again appointed Grand Household Minister and promoted Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: [34] He returned as Grand Household Minister and rose to Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 尋李傕作亂，嵩亦病卒，贈驃騎將軍印綬，拜家一人為郎。

translations.literal: Soon Li Jue rebelled; Song also died of illness. He was posthumously awarded the seal ribbon of General of Agile Cavalry, and one member of his household was appointed a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Jue rose; Song died sick. The court gave him the posthumous rank of General of Agile Cavalry and ennobled one kinsman as a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 嵩為人愛慎盡勤，前後上表陳諫有補益者五百餘事，皆手書毀草，不宣於外。

translations.literal: Song was by nature careful and diligent; he submitted more than five hundred memorials of remonstrance that proved beneficial, all drafted in his own hand and the drafts destroyed so nothing spread abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Song was meticulous: over five hundred memorials that helped policy passed under his brush, each rough copy burned so gossip never saw them.

sentences.zh: 又折節下士，門無留客。

translations.literal: He also humbled himself before scholars and turned no caller from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He humbled himself before talent and kept his gate open past dusk.

sentences.zh: [35]時人皆稱而附之。

translations.literal: [35] Men of the time praised him and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: [35] Contemporaries sang his virtues and flocked to his door.

sentences.zh: 堅壽亦顯名，後為侍中，辭不拜，病卒。

translations.literal: Jianshou also achieved renown; later he was appointed Palace Attendant but declined the office and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Jianshou won fame too; offered Palace Attendant, he refused and died in bed.

sentences.zh: 朱儁，字公偉，會稽上虞人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Jun, courtesy name Gongwei, was a native of Shangyu in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jun, styled Gongwei, came from Shangyu in Kuaiji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少孤，母嘗販繒為業。

translations.literal: He lost his father young; his mother dealt in silk for a living.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he was raised by a mother who peddled silk.

sentences.zh: 儁以孝養致名，為縣門下書佐，好義輕財，鄉閭敬之。

translations.literal: Jun earned a name through filial devotion in supporting her; he served as clerical aide at the county gate, loved righteousness and treated wealth lightly, and his village respected him.
translations.idiomatic: He won notice for supporting her with filial care, clerked at the county office, prized honor over coin, and neighbors tipped their hats.

sentences.zh: 時同郡周規辟公府，當行，假郡庫錢百萬，以為冠幘費，而後倉卒督責，規家貧無以備，儁乃竊母繒帛，為規解對。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman, Zhou Gui, was summoned to the Excellencies’ offices and was about to depart; he borrowed a million cash from the commandery treasury for cap and turban expenses, but afterward sudden pressure came for repayment; Gui’s family was poor and could not supply it, so Jun secretly took his mother’s silk bolts to settle Gui’s account.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Gui of the same county took a capital appointment he borrowed a million from the county vault for travel gear; sudden dunning followed and his kin could not pay—Jun stole his mother’s silk to clear Zhou’s debt.

sentences.zh: [36]母既失產業，深恚責之。

translations.literal: [36] Once his mother lost her stock she bitterly reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: [36] When she discovered the empty chest she scolded him furiously.

sentences.zh: 儁曰：「小損當大益，初貧後富，必然理也。」

translations.literal: Jun said: ‘A small loss today brings great gain later; poor at first, rich afterward—that is the sure pattern.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘Small loss, large gain,’ he said; ‘start poor, end rich—that is how heaven balances accounts.’

sentences.zh: 本縣長山陽度尚見而奇之，薦於太守韋毅，稍歷郡職。

translations.literal: The county magistrate, Du Shang of Shanyang, saw this and marveled; he recommended Jun to Administrator Wei Yi, and Jun gradually advanced through commandery posts.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Du Shang of Shanyang spotted the deed, praised him to Prefect Wei Yi, and Jun climbed the local ladder rung by rung.

sentences.zh: 後太守尹端以儁為主簿。

translations.literal: Later Administrator Yin Duan appointed Jun chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yin Duan later made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 熹平二年，端坐討賊許昭失利，為州所奏，罪應棄市。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiping, when Duan campaigned against the rebel Xu Zhao and suffered defeat, the province memorialized against him; by statute he deserved execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiping 2 Yin Duan attacked bandit Xu Zhao, lost, and the province indicted him for public execution.

sentences.zh: 儁乃羸服閒行，輕繼數百金到京師，賂主章吏，遂得刊定州奏，故端得輸作左校。

translations.literal: Jun donned worn clothes and traveled secretly, carrying several hundred in gold to the capital, bribed the clerk who handled memorials, and thereby secured revision of the provincial report so Duan was sentenced only to labor in the Left Arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: Jun slipped to Luoyang in rags with a few hundred in gold, greased the memorial office, and had the charge softened to penal labor at the Left Arsenal.

sentences.zh: 端喜於降免而不知其由，儁亦終無所言。

translations.literal: Duan rejoiced at the reduced sentence without knowing the cause; Jun never spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Duan thanked fortune and never learned who bought his life; Jun kept silent forever.

sentences.zh: 後太守徐珪舉儁孝廉，再遷除蘭陵令，政有異能，為東海相所表。

translations.literal: Later Administrator Xu Gui nominated Jun Filial and Incorrupt; after two promotions he was appointed magistrate of Lanling; his administration showed unusual ability and was cited by the Chancellor of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Xu Gui recommended him Filial and Incorrupt; two steps up he governed Lanling with such skill that the Donghai chancellor memorialized him.

sentences.zh: 會交址部腢賊並起，牧守剁弱不能禁。

translations.literal: At that time bandits arose everywhere in Jiao Province while governors and shepherds proved too weak to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Jiao Province boiled with rebels and civil governors lacked steel to stop them.

sentences.zh: 又交址賊梁龍等萬餘人，與南海太守孔芝反叛，攻破郡縣。

translations.literal: Moreover bandits of Jiao such as Liang Long, over ten thousand strong, rebelled with Administrator Kong Zhi of Nanhai and smashed county seats.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Long of Jiao led ten thousand men alongside Nanhai prefect Kong Zhi and tore through the delta towns.

sentences.zh: 光和元年，即拜儁交址刺史，令過本郡簡募家兵及所調，[37]合五千人，分從兩道而入。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guanghe Jun was appointed Inspector of Jiao with orders to pass through his home commandery to recruit household troops and levies, [37] totaling five thousand men, advancing by two routes.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghe 1 named him Inspector of Jiao; he detoured home to raise household veterans and drafted militia—[37] five thousand in all—in two columns.

sentences.zh: 既到州界，按甲不前，先遣使詣郡，觀賊虛實，宣揚威德，以震動其心；

translations.literal: Once inside the province he halted armor and did not advance; first he sent envoys to the commanderies to observe rebel strength, proclaim awe and virtue, and shake their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he held his lines, sent scouts into each commandery to measure the enemy and broadcast imperial majesty,

sentences.zh: 既而與七郡兵俱進逼之，遂斬梁龍，降者數萬人，旬月盡定。

translations.literal: then advanced shoulder to shoulder with troops from seven commanderies, pressed the rebels, beheaded Liang Long, and tens of thousands surrendered; within a month all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: then marched with seven commanderies’ levies, struck Liang Long dead, and accepted tens of thousands of surrenders—a quiet province within weeks.

sentences.zh: 以功封都亭侯，千五百戶，賜黃金五十斤，徵為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed marquis of Ducheng at fifteen hundred households, awarded fifty catties of gold, and summoned as Grandee Remonstrant.
translations.idiomatic: The throne made him Marquis of Ducheng at fifteen hundred households, poured fifty catties of gold into his lap, and recalled him as Grandee Remonstrant.

sentences.zh: 及黃巾起，公卿多薦儁有才略，拜為右中郎將，持節，與左中郎將皇甫嵩討穎川、汝南、陳國諸賊，悉破平之。

translations.literal: When the Yellow Turbans rose, Excellencies widely recommended Jun’s talent and strategy; he was appointed General of the Household on the Right, given credentials, and with General of the Household on the Left Huangfu Song campaigned against bandits in Yingchuan, Runan, and Chen, routing every band.
translations.idiomatic: As Turbans flared, ministers praised his gifts; he became General of the Household on the Right with imperial baton, paired with Huangfu Song on the left, and swept Yingchuan, Runan, and Chen clean.

sentences.zh: 嵩乃上言其狀，而以功歸儁，於是進封西鄉侯，遷鎮賊中郎將。

translations.literal: Song then memorialized the facts but credited the achievements to Jun; Jun was therefore advanced to marquis of Xixiang and promoted General Who Suppresses Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Song reported victory yet handed the glory to Jun, who gained Marquis of Xixiang and the title General Who Suppresses Bandits.

sentences.zh: 時南陽黃巾張曼成起兵，稱「神上使」，衆數萬，殺郡守褚貢，屯宛下百餘日。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Mancheng of the Nanyang Yellow Turbans rose, styled himself ‘Divine Envoy Above,’ massed tens of thousands, killed Prefect Chu Gong, and camped beneath Wan for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanyang, Zhang Mancheng styled himself ‘Supernal Herald,’ slaughtered Prefect Chu Gong, and besieged Wan for months with tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 後太守秦頡擊殺曼成，賊更以趙弘為帥，衆浸盛，遂十餘萬，據宛城。

translations.literal: Later Prefect Qin Jie attacked and killed Mancheng; the rebels chose Zhao Hong as leader; their numbers swelled past a hundred thousand and they seized Wan city.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Qin Jie slew Mancheng; the bands raised Zhao Hong until over a hundred thousand held the walls of Wan.

sentences.zh: 儁與荊州刺史徐璆及秦頡合兵萬八千人圍弘，自六月至八月不拔。

translations.literal: Jun joined Inspector Xu Qiu of Jing Province and Qin Jie with eighteen thousand men to besiege Hong from the sixth month through the eighth without taking the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, Inspector Xu Qiu, and Qin Jie brought eighteen thousand to invest Zhao Hong from summer into autumn without a breach.

sentences.zh: 有司奏欲征儁。

translations.literal: Responsible officials memorialized to recall Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry urged his recall.

sentences.zh: 司空張溫上疏曰：「昔秦用白起，燕任樂毅，皆曠年歷載，乃能克敵。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Wen submitted a memorial: ‘Formerly Qin employed Bai Qi and Yan entrusted Yue Yi—both needed years before enemies yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Wen argued: ‘Qin needed Bai Qi and Yan needed Yue Yi—years passed before victory.’

sentences.zh: [38]儁討穎川，以有功效，引師南指，方略已設，臨軍易將，兵家所忌，宜假日月，責其成功。

translations.literal: [38] Jun campaigned in Yingchuan with proven success; his army points south, plans are fixed—to swap generals on the eve of battle is what strategists dread; grant him months and demand results.
translations.idiomatic: [38] Jun proved himself in Yingchuan; his southern thrust is set—changing captains midstream invites defeat; give him time and hold him to outcome.’

sentences.zh: 」靈帝乃止。

translations.literal: ’ Emperor Ling therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling dropped the recall.

sentences.zh: 儁因急擊弘，斬之。

translations.literal: Jun then pressed the assault fiercely, killed Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Jun hammered the walls and struck Zhao Hong down.

sentences.zh: 賊餘帥韓忠復據宛拒儁。

translations.literal: The surviving chief Han Zhong again held Wan and resisted Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant Han Zhong reopened Wan against him.

sentences.zh: 儁兵少不敵，乃張圍結壘，起土山以臨城內，因鳴鼓攻其西南，賊悉衆赴之。

translations.literal: Jun’s troops were too few to match them, so he spread the siege, linked ramparts, raised earthen hills overlooking the interior, then beat drums and attacked the southwest so the rebels rushed their entire force there.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, he ringed the city, piled siege mounds, drummed the southwest wall until every defender rushed thither,

sentences.zh: 儁自將精卒五千，掩其東北，乘城而入。

translations.literal: Jun himself led five thousand picked troops to strike the northeast, scaled the walls, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: then led five thousand elites up the northeast parapet and poured inside.

sentences.zh: 忠乃退保小城，惶懼乞降。

translations.literal: Zhong then withdrew to hold a lesser enclosure, terrified and begging to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhong shrank into the inner citadel, begging terms with shaking voice.

sentences.zh: 司馬張超及徐璆、秦頡皆欲聽之。

translations.literal: Major Zhang Chao together with Xu Qiu and Qin Jie all wished to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Major Zhang Chao, Xu Qiu, and Qin Jie voted to accept.

sentences.zh: 儁曰：「兵有形同而埶異者。

translations.literal: Jun said: ‘War admits forms that look alike yet circumstances differ.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, ‘Two battles may look alike yet demand opposite answers.’

sentences.zh: 昔秦項之際，民無定主，故賞附以勸來耳。

translations.literal: In the age of Qin and Xiang Yu the people had no settled lord; therefore rewarding submission encouraged newcomers.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin and Chu tore the realm apart, rewarding defectors bought allies.’

sentences.zh: 今海內一統，唯黃巾造寇，納降無以勸善，討之足以懲惡。

translations.literal: Now within the seas there is unity; only the Yellow Turbans make rebellion—to welcome surrender does not encourage good, while crushing them suffices to punish evil.
translations.idiomatic: Today the empire is one; only Turbans revolt—pardons teach nothing, but the sword teaches fear.’

sentences.zh: 今若受之，更開逆意，賊利則進戰，鈍則乞降，縱敵長寇，非良計也。

translations.literal: If we accept them now we only widen their defiance: when fighting suits them they advance, when blunt they beg mercy—indulging the foe breeds banditry; it is no sound plan.
translations.idiomatic: Grant terms now and every rebel learns to fight while winning and kneel while losing—you would nurse the next rising.’

sentences.zh: 」因急攻，連戰不克。

translations.literal: ’ He therefore pressed the attack fiercely; battle after battle failed to crack them.
translations.idiomatic: He refused and pressed harder, yet the inner wall held.

sentences.zh: 儁登土山望之，顧謂張超曰：「吾知之矣。

translations.literal: Jun climbed the earth hill to observe, looked back at Zhang Chao and said: ‘I understand them now.
translations.idiomatic: From the mound he told Zhang Chao, ‘I see their bind.’

sentences.zh: 賊今外圍周固，內營逼急，乞降不受，欲出不得，所以死戰也。

translations.literal: The rebels now have their outer ring intact and their inner camp pressed tight; we refuse surrender yet grant no outlet—they therefore fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Their outer lines are iron, their inner yards suffocate; we deny surrender and escape—so they fight like cornered wolves.’

sentences.zh: 萬人一心，猶不可當，況十萬乎！

translations.literal: When ten thousand share one mind they cannot be withstood—how much more a hundred thousand!
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand of one heart cannot be stopped—what of a hundred thousand?’

sentences.zh: 其害甚矣。

translations.literal: The harm would be extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The butcher’s bill would choke heaven.’

sentences.zh: 不如徹圍，並兵入城。

translations.literal: Better lift the siege and combine troops inside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Better open a seam and slip our strength within.’

sentences.zh: 忠見圍解，埶必自出，出則意散，易破之道也。

translations.literal: When Zhong sees the siege loosen his posture will surely drive him out; once outside his intent scatters—that is the easy road to break him.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Zhong sees a gap he will sortie; outside the walls discipline breaks—that is when we cut him down.’

sentences.zh: 」既而解圍，忠果出戰，儁因擊，大破之。

translations.literal: ’ He then raised the siege; Zhong indeed sallied forth and Jun attacked and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: He drew the ring wide; Han Zhong charged out and Jun shattered him.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐北數十里，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: Pressing the pursuit northward for several tens of li, he took more than ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The chase ran dozens of li and left ten thousand heads for the crows.

sentences.zh: 忠等遂降。

translations.literal: Zhong and his fellows then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhong capitulated.

sentences.zh: 而秦頡積忿忠，遂殺之。

translations.literal: But Qin Jie nursed old hatred toward Zhong and therefore killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jie’s old grudge moved him to murder the prisoner.

sentences.zh: 餘衆懼不自安，復以孫夏為帥，還屯宛中。

translations.literal: The remnant host feared for itself; again they made Sun Xia leader and returned to camp inside Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors trembled, raised Sun Xia, and barricaded Wan anew.

sentences.zh: 儁急攻之。

translations.literal: Jun attacked urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Jun stormed the walls again.

sentences.zh: 夏走，追至西鄂精山，又破之。

translations.literal: Xia fled; Jun pursued to Mount Jing west of Xi'e and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xia bolted; Jun ran him to Mount Jing west of Xi'e and broke him a second time.

sentences.zh: [39]復斬萬餘級，賊遂解散。

translations.literal: [39] He again took more than ten thousand heads and the bandits then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: [39] Another ten thousand heads fell and the rebellion dissolved.

sentences.zh: 明年春，遣使者持節拜儁右車騎將軍，振旅還京師，以為光祿大夫，增邑五千，更封錢塘侯，[40]加位特進。

translations.literal: The next spring an envoy with imperial credentials appointed Jun General of Chariots and Cavalry on the Right; he marched back to the capital in triumph, was made Grand Household Minister, given five thousand additional households, re-enfeoffed as marquis of Qiantang, [40] and granted the honorary rank of Exceptional Merit.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring baton-bearing envoys named him General of Chariots and Cavalry on the Right; he brought the army home, took Grand Household Minister, gained five thousand extra households, became Marquis of Qiantang, [40] and received ‘Exceptional Merit’ precedence.

sentences.zh: 以母喪去官，起家，復為將作大匠，轉少府、太僕。

translations.literal: He left office for mourning his mother; later he was recalled as Superintendent of the Imperial Clan, then transferred to Privy Treasurer and Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: Maternal mourning pulled him down; recall raised him Superintendent of the Imperial Clan, then Privy Treasurer, then Coachman.

sentences.zh: 自黃巾賊後，復有黑山、黃龍、白波、左校、郭大賢、於氐根、青牛角、張白騎、劉石、左髭丈八、平漢、大計、司隸、掾哉、[41]雷公、浮雲、飛燕、白雀、楊鳳、於毒、五鹿、李大目、白繞、畦固、苦唒之徒，[42]並起山谷閒，不可勝數。

translations.literal: After the Yellow Turbans came Black Mountain, Yellow Dragon, White Wave, Left School, Guo Daxian, Yu Digēn, Qing Niujiao, Zhang Baiqi, Liu Shi, Left Beard Eight Feet, Ping Han, Daji, Director of Retainers, Clerk Zai, [41] Leigong, Fuyun, Feiyan, Baique, Yang Feng, Yu Du, Wulu, Li Damu, Bai Rao, Gui Gu, Kushēng, and others—[42] rising together among mountain valleys beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the Turbans rose Black Mountain, Yellow Dragon, White Wave, Left School, Guo Daxian, Yu Digēn, Qing Niujiao, Zhang Baiqi, Liu Shi, Left-Zī Eight-Foot, Ping Han, Grand Clerk, Metropolitan Clerk Zai, [41] Thunder Duke, Drifting Cloud, Flying Swallow, White Sparrow, Yang Feng, Yu Du, Wulu, Big-Eye Li, Bai Rao, Gui Gu, Bitter-Shriek, [42]—hosts beyond numbering in the hills.

sentences.zh: 其大聲者稱雷公，騎白馬者為張白騎，輕便者言飛燕，多髭者號於氐根，[43]大眼者為大目，如此稱號，各有所因。

translations.literal: Those with loud voices called themselves Thunder Duke; riders on white horses were Zhang Baiqi; agile ones called themselves Flying Swallow; men with heavy beards styled themselves Yu Digēn; [43] big-eyed men were called Big Eye—such titles each had some origin.
translations.idiomatic: [43] Loud shouters were ‘Thunder Duke,’ white horse riders ‘Zhang Baiqi,’ foot-quick men ‘Flying Swallow,’ bushy-bearded bands ‘Yu Digēn,’ wide-eyed chiefs ‘Big Eye’—every nickname had its tale.

sentences.zh: 大者二三萬，小者六七千。

translations.literal: Large bands numbered twenty or thirty thousand; small ones six or seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Major camps counted twenty or thirty thousand blades; minor ones six or seven thousand.

sentences.zh: 賊帥常山人張燕，輕勇趫捷，故軍中號曰飛燕。

translations.literal: The Changshan bandit chief Zhang Yan was nimble and brave; the army therefore nicknamed him Flying Swallow.
translations.idiomatic: Changshan’s Zhang Yan was lightning on his feet—troops dubbed him Flying Swallow.

sentences.zh: 善得士卒心，乃與中山、常山、趙郡、上黨、河內諸山谷寇賊更相交通，衆至*

translations.literal: Skilled at winning his troops’ devotion, he forged ties among the ravine bandits of Zhongshan, Changshan, Zhao commandery, Shangdang, and Henei, and their masses grew until they reached—
translations.idiomatic: He bound his soldiers with loyalty and coordinated every hill stronghold from Zhongshan to Henei until their numbers mounted toward—

translations.literal: (The manuscript gloss reads bo ‘elder,’ editors emend to bǎi ‘hundred.’)
translations.idiomatic: (Critical note: graph should read ‘hundred,’ not ‘elder brother.’)

sentences.zh: **[百]*萬，號曰黑山賊。

translations.literal: **[one]** million strong; they were styled the Black Mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: They swelled past a million blades and earned the name Black Mountain rebels.

sentences.zh: 河北諸郡縣並被其害，朝廷不能討。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties north of the Yellow River were alike ravaged; the court could not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Every district north of the great river burned while Luoyang mustered no answer.

sentences.zh: 燕乃遣使至京師，奏書乞降，遂拜燕平難中郎將，使領河北諸山谷事，歲得舉孝廉、計吏。

translations.literal: Yan therefore sent envoys to the capital with a memorial offering surrender; he was appointed General of the Household Who Pacifies Disturbances, charged with affairs of the Hebei mountain valleys, and allowed annual nominations of Filial and Incorrupt men and accounting clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan sued for peace, won General Who Pacifies Crisis, superintended the northern hills, and kept yearly rights to recommend Filial-and-Incorrupt candidates and fiscal clerks.

sentences.zh: 燕後漸寇河內，逼近京師，於是出儁為河內太守，將家兵擊却之。

translations.literal: Later Yan gradually raided Henei and pressed close to the capital; Jun was therefore sent out as Administrator of Henei and led household troops to beat him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yan probed Henei and threatened the throne, Zhu Jun took that prefecture and repelled him with family retainers.

sentences.zh: 其後諸賊多為袁紹所定，事在紹傳。

translations.literal: Afterward most of the bandits were subdued by Yuan Shao; the matter is treated in Shao’s biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao later crushed most of those bands—see his chapter.

sentences.zh: 復拜儁為光祿大夫，轉屯騎，尋拜城門校尉、河南尹。

translations.literal: Jun was again appointed Grand Household Minister, transferred to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, soon appointed Colonel of the City Gates and Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rotated back through Grand Household Minister and Garrison Cavalry to City Gates colonel and Henan governor.

sentences.zh: 時董卓擅政，以儁宿將，外甚親納而心實忌之。

translations.literal: At that time Dong Zhuo monopolized government; although toward Jun, a veteran general, he seemed cordial on the surface, inwardly he feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo ran the court; toward Jun the old warhorse he smiled in public and worried in private.

sentences.zh: 及關東兵盛，卓懼，數請公卿會議，徙都長安，儁輒止之。

translations.literal: When the armies east of the passes grew strong Zhuo became afraid and repeatedly summoned dukes and ministers to conference on removing the capital to Chang’an; Jun always blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: As the eastern league grew, Zhuo summoned ministers again and again to debate moving west—Jun blocked every session.

sentences.zh: 卓雖惡儁異己，然貪其名重，乃表遷太僕，以為己副。

translations.literal: Though Zhuo hated Jun for opposing him, he coveted his great reputation and therefore memorialized to promote him Coachman, making him his own deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo hated the obstruction yet wanted Jun’s prestige, so he nominated him Coachman as nominal lieutenant.

sentences.zh: 使者拜，儁辭不肯受。

translations.literal: When the envoy invested him with office Jun declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial messenger offered the seal; Jun refused it.

sentences.zh: 因曰：「國家西遷，必孤天下之望，以成山東之釁，臣不見其可也。

translations.literal: He therefore said: ‘If the state moves west it will surely disappoint All Under Heaven and feed strife east of the mountains—I do not see how that can be right.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Shift the court west,’ he said, ‘and you orphan every loyal heart while handing Shandong a banner—I see no wisdom there.’

sentences.zh: 」使者詰曰：「召君受拜而君拒之，不問徙事而君陳之，其故何也？

translations.literal: ’ The envoy demanded: ‘You were summoned to receive appointment yet you refuse; without being asked about the removal you argue against it—what is your reason?
translations.idiomatic: The envoy pressed: ‘You were called to office yet resist; nobody consulted you on moving the capital yet you preach—why?’

sentences.zh: 」儁曰：「副相國，非臣所堪也；

translations.literal: ’ Jun said: ‘To serve as deputy to the Imperial Chancellor is beyond what this subject can bear;
translations.idiomatic: Jun replied, ‘Deputy to the Chancellor exceeds my strength.’

sentences.zh: 遷都計，非事所急也。

translations.literal: a plan to move the capital is not what pressing affairs require.
translations.idiomatic: Uprooting Luoyang solves no urgent ill.’

sentences.zh: 辭所不堪，言所非急，臣之宜也。

translations.literal: Declining what I cannot bear and speaking against what is not urgent—that is what befits a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Refusing what outmatches me and faulting what can wait—that is how a servant should speak.’

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「遷都之事，不聞其計，就有未露，何所承受？

translations.literal: ’ The envoy said: ‘On the matter of moving the capital I have heard no such plan; even if something unrevealed exists, how did you come to know it?
translations.idiomatic: ‘Who spoke of the western move?’ asked the envoy. ‘No such edict has aired.’

sentences.zh: 」儁曰：「相國董卓具為臣說，所以知耳。」

translations.literal: ’ Jun said: ‘Imperial Chancellor Dong Zhuo explained it fully to me—that is how I know.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘Chancellor Dong Zhuo told me himself,’ said Jun—that is my source.’

sentences.zh: 使人不能屈，由是止不為副。

translations.literal: Envoys could not bend him; therefore the deputy appointment stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys yielded; Zhuo dropped the deputy appointment.

sentences.zh: 卓後入關，留儁守洛陽，而儁與山東諸將通謀為內應。

translations.literal: Later Zhuo entered the passes and left Jun to guard Luoyang, while Jun conspired with eastern commanders as an inside contact.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuo marched through the passes he left Jun in Luoyang; Jun plotted with the eastern alliance as their man inside.

sentences.zh: 既而懼為卓所襲，乃棄官奔荊州。

translations.literal: Soon fearing Zhuo would strike him, he abandoned office and fled to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Zhuo’s knives, he shed his seals and fled south into Jing.

sentences.zh: 卓以弘農楊懿為河南尹，守洛陽。

translations.literal: Zhuo appointed Yang Yi of Hongnong Governor of Henan to hold Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo named Yang Yi of Hongnong Henan governor to hold the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 儁聞，復進兵還洛，懿走。

translations.literal: When Jun heard this he again advanced his army back to Luoyang; Yi fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jun marched back on word of Yang Yi; the placeholder governor ran.

sentences.zh: 儁以河南殘破無所資，乃東屯中牟，移書州郡，請師討卓。

translations.literal: Because Henan lay in ruins and offered no supplies, Jun camped east at Zhongmou and sent letters to provinces and commanderies requesting troops to punish Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Henan was stripped bare—Jun quartered at Zhongmou, mailed every governor, and begged levies against Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史陶謙遣精兵三千，餘州郡稍有所給，謙乃上儁行車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Inspector Tao Qian of Xu Province sent three thousand picked troops; other provinces and commanderies contributed modestly, whereupon Qian memorialized to appoint Jun acting General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian sent three thousand elites; other jurisdictions trickled aid until Tao petitioned Jun as acting General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 董卓聞之，使其將李傕、郭汜等數萬人屯河南拒儁。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo heard this he sent his generals Li Jue, Guo Si, and others—several tens of thousands—to camp south of the river to oppose Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo countered by posting Li Jue and Guo Si with tens of thousands south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 儁逆擊，為傕、汜所破。

translations.literal: Jun met them in attack but was broken by Jue and Si.
translations.idiomatic: Jun attacked and was shattered by Li and Guo.

sentences.zh: 儁自知不敵，留關下不敢復前。

translations.literal: Jun knew himself no match and halted below the passes, not daring to advance again.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the odds, he hugged the barrier forts and advanced no farther.

sentences.zh: 及董卓被誅，傕、汜作亂，儁時猶在中牟。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo was executed and Jue and Si made turmoil, Jun was still at Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuo died and Li–Guo seized Chang’an, Jun remained at Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 陶謙以儁名臣，數有戰功，可委以大事，乃與諸豪桀共推儁為太師，因移檄牧伯，同討李傕等，奉迎天子。

translations.literal: Tao Qian considered Jun a renowned minister who had repeatedly won battles and could be entrusted with great affairs; together with various champions he urged Jun as Grand Tutor, issued proclamations to shepherds and governors, and jointly campaigned against Li Jue and the others to welcome the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian deemed Jun a famed commander fit for great trust and, with regional strongmen, acclaimed him Grand Tutor, circulated summons to every governor, and vowed to crush Li Jue and welcome the emperor.

sentences.zh: 乃奏記於儁曰：「徐州刺史陶謙、前楊州刺史周干、琅邪相陰德、東海相劉馗、[44]彭城相汲廉、北海相孔融、沛相袁忠、太山太守應劭、汝南太守徐璆、前九江太守服虔、博士鄭玄等，敢言之行車騎將軍河南尹莫府：[45]國家既遭董卓，重以李傕、郭汜之禍，幼主劫執，忠良殘敝，長安隔絕，不知吉凶。

translations.literal: They therefore submitted a memorial to Jun: ‘Inspector Tao Qian of Xu Province, former Inspector Zhou Gan of Yang Province, Chancellor Yinde of Langye, Chancellor Liu Kui of Donghai, [44] Chancellor Ji Lian of Pengcheng, Chancellor Kong Rong of Beihai, Chancellor Yuan Zhong of Pei, Administrator Ying Shao of Taishan, Administrator Xu Qiu of Runan, former Administrator Fu Qian of Jiujiang, Erudite Zheng Xuan, and others venture to address the acting General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Henan at headquarters: [45] the state has already suffered Dong Zhuo and, doubly, the disaster of Li Jue and Guo Si; the young sovereign is held hostage, loyal men are broken, Chang’an is cut off and we know not whether it stands or falls.
translations.idiomatic: They wrote: ‘We—Tao Qian, Zhou Gan, Yinde, Liu Kui, [44] Ji Lian, Kong Rong, Yuan Zhong, Ying Shao, Xu Qiu, Fu Qian, Zheng Xuan—address your headquarters: Zhuo wounded us, Li Jue and Guo Si wound us again; the boy emperor is hostage, loyalists lie in shards, and Chang’an’s fate is unknown.’

sentences.zh: 是以臨官尹人，搢紳有識，莫不憂懼，以為自非明哲雄霸之士，曷能克濟禍亂！

translations.literal: Therefore incumbent officials and gentry of insight are alike fearful, believing that unless a wise, enlightened, and heroic hegemon appears, who can settle such calamity!
translations.idiomatic: Every serving officer with insight asks what sage-warlord can heal this wound.’

sentences.zh: 自起兵已來，於茲三年，州郡轉相顧望，未有奮擊之功，而互爭私變，更相疑惑。

translations.literal: Since armies rose it has been three years; provinces and commanderies watch one another without daring a decisive blow, while wrangling private quarrels and doubting each other.
translations.idiomatic: Three years of war bands have passed; governors eye one another, strike no telling blow, and tear at private feuds.’

sentences.zh: 謙等並共諮諏，議消國難。

translations.literal: Qian and the rest jointly consulted on ending the national crisis.
translations.idiomatic: We gathered to draft a cure for the dynasty.’

sentences.zh: 僉曰：『將軍君侯，既文且武，應運而出，凡百君子，靡不顒顒。

translations.literal: All said: “Lord General, both cultured and martial, answered heaven’s summons; every gentleman bows in longing.
translations.idiomatic: All said: “You marry letters to arms; fate raised you; every gentleman cranes toward you.”

sentences.zh: 』故相率厲，簡選精悍，堪能深入，直指咸陽，多持資糧，足支半歲，謹同心腹，委之元帥。

translations.literal: ” Therefore they jointly urged themselves, picked stalwart fighters able to strike deep, aiming straight at Xianyang, laid in provisions enough for half a year, and with one heart entrusted their lives to the supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: So we steeled ourselves, chose shock troops for a drive on Xianyang, stocked six months’ grain, and pledged life and fortune to you as commander-in-chief.”

sentences.zh: 」會李傕用太尉周忠、尚書賈詡策，征儁入朝。

translations.literal: ’ Just then Li Jue, adopting the strategy of Grand Commandant Zhou Zhong and Minister Secretary Jia Xu, summoned Jun to court.
translations.idiomatic: Before plans matured Li Jue—on Zhou Zhong’s and Jia Xu’s counsel—summoned Jun to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 軍吏皆憚入關，欲應陶謙等。

translations.literal: Army clerks all dreaded entering the passes and wished to answer Tao Qian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Jun’s officers feared the barrier and urged joining Tao Qian.

sentences.zh: 儁曰：「以君召臣，義不俟駕，[46]況天子詔乎！

translations.literal: Jun said: ‘When the lord summons his minister, propriety does not await the harnessing of horses—[46] how much less an imperial edict!
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, ‘The lord calls and the servant does not wait to harness—[46] how much more when the edict bears the throne’s seal!’

sentences.zh: 且傕、汜小豎，樊稠庸兒，無他遠略，又埶力相敵，變難必作。

translations.literal: Moreover Jue and Si are petty fellows; Fan Chou is a mediocrity; they harbor no grand designs and their strengths balance each other—crisis and mutiny are sure to arise.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Guo Si are alley soldiers; Fan Chou is blunt iron; matched in greed they will soon turn on each other.’

sentences.zh: 吾乘其閒，大事可濟。

translations.literal: If I exploit their intervals the great affair can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Exploit their cracks and Han may rise.’

sentences.zh: 」遂辭謙議而就傕征，復為太僕，謙等遂罷。

translations.literal: ’ He therefore declined Qian’s plan and obeyed Jue’s summons, again becoming Coachman; Qian and the others then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He spurned Tao Qian, obeyed Li Jue, resumed the Coachmanship, and the eastern league dissolved.

sentences.zh: 初平四年，代周忠為太尉，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chuping he replaced Zhou Zhong as Grand Commandant and supervised Minister Secretary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chuping 4 promoted him Grand Commandant over Zhou Zhong with Secretariat oversight.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，以日食免，復行驃騎將軍事，持節鎮關東。

translations.literal: The next autumn he was dismissed because of a solar eclipse; again he acted as General of Agile Cavalry with credentials to secure the region east of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Next autumn an eclipse cost him his post; he became acting General of Agile Cavalry with baton to pacify the east.

sentences.zh: 未發，會李傕殺樊稠，而郭汜又自疑，與傕相攻，長安中亂，故儁止不出，留拜大司農。

translations.literal: Before he could depart Li Jue killed Fan Chou while Guo Si grew suspicious and attacked Jue; Chang’an fell into chaos, so Jun halted and did not go out; he was retained as Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he marched Li Jue slew Fan Chou; Guo Si attacked Li Jue and Chang’an boiled—Jun stayed, took Minister of Agriculture, and never crossed the pass.

sentences.zh: 獻帝詔儁與太尉楊彪等十餘人譬郭汜，令與李傕和。

translations.literal: Emperor Xian ordered Jun together with Grand Commandant Yang Biao and more than ten others to persuade Guo Si to make peace with Li Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian sent Jun with Yang Biao and a dozen ministers to coax Guo Si toward peace with Li Jue.

sentences.zh: 汜不肯，遂留質儁等。

translations.literal: Si refused and therefore detained Jun and the others as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si refused and held Jun’s party hostage.

sentences.zh: 儁素剛，即日發病卒。

translations.literal: Jun was by nature rigidly upright; that same day he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jun’s spine was steel; rage and shame struck him dead the same day.

sentences.zh: 子皓，亦有才行，官至豫章太守。

translations.literal: His son Hao also had talent and conduct; he rose to Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Hao matched him in gifts and governed Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 論曰：皇甫嵩、朱儁並以上將之略，受脤倉卒之時。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun alike possessed the strategy of supreme commanders and received sacrificial meat in an hour of sudden crisis.
translations.idiomatic: The historian’s verdict: Song and Jun bore marshal-class minds when crisis handed them the axe.

sentences.zh: [47]及其功成師克，威聲滿天下。

translations.literal: [47] When their merit stood complete and armies triumphed, awe-inspiring fame filled All Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: [47] Victory crowned them and awe filled the realm.

sentences.zh: 值弱主蒙塵，獷賊放命，斯誠葉公投袂之幾，翟義鞠旅之日，[48]故梁衍獻規，山東連盟，而捨格天之大業，蹈匹夫之小諒，卒狼狽虎口，為智士笑。

translations.literal: Yet when a feeble sovereign wandered in dust and brutal rebels defied heaven’s command, this was truly the moment for Duke Ye to fling his sleeve and the day for Zhai Yi to marshal his hosts—[48] hence Liang Yan offered counsel and Shandong forged alliances; yet they abandoned heaven-spanning enterprise and trod the petty scruples of common men, ending in disarray within the tiger’s jaws, mocked by men of insight.
translations.idiomatic: [48] Yet when the boy emperor wandered and wolves held the capital—the hour Ye Gong cast his sleeve, the day Zhai Yi beat the drum—they heard Liang Yan and Shandong’s oaths yet clung to common scruples, forsook heaven-high deed, and stumbled into the tiger’s mouth for wise men to mock.

sentences.zh: [49]豈天之長斯亂也？

translations.literal: [49] Did Heaven mean to prolong such chaos?
translations.idiomatic: [49] Did Heaven mean to stretch this night?’

sentences.zh: 何智勇之不終甚乎！

translations.literal: How utterly their wisdom and courage failed to reach the end!
translations.idiomatic: How shallow courage proved when the road turned long!’

sentences.zh: 前史晉平原華嶠，稱其父光祿大夫表，[50]每言其祖魏太尉歆[51]稱「時人說皇甫嵩之不伐，汝豫之戰，歸功朱儁，張角之捷，本之於盧植，收名斂策，而己不有焉。
