translations.literal: Earlier historian Hua Qiao of Pingyuan in Jin observed that his father, Grand Household Minister Hua Biao, [50] often said his grandfather, Wei Grand Commandant Hua Xin, [51] reported that men of the age praised Huangfu Song for not boasting: in the battles of Ru and Yu he credited Zhu Jun; in the victory over Zhang Jiao he traced the root to Lu Zhi—gathering renown while folding his strategies, keeping nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s Hua Qiao recalls his father Hua Biao quoting grandfather Hua Xin: contemporaries said Song never crowed—Ru–Yu glory he gave Jun, Zhang Jiao’s fall he traced to Lu Zhi—he wore fame yet hid every stratagem.’

sentences.zh: [52]蓋功名者，世之所甚重也。

translations.literal: [52] Achievement and fame are what the age esteems most deeply.
translations.idiomatic: [52] Glory is what the world squeezes hardest.’

sentences.zh: 誠能不爭天下之所甚重，則怨禍不深矣」。

translations.literal: If one can truly refrain from contending for what the world esteems most deeply, then resentment and disaster will not run deep.’
translations.idiomatic: Refuse that prize and malice lacks teeth.’

sentences.zh: 如皇甫公之赴履危亂，而能終以歸全者，其致不亦貴乎！

translations.literal: For one like Lord Huangfu who walked through peril and chaos yet finished with integrity preserved—is not such attainment precious!
translations.idiomatic: To cross chaos like Song and finish with name and body whole—that jewel shines rare.’

sentences.zh: 故顏子願不伐善為先，斯亦行身之要與！

translations.literal: Therefore Yan Hui placed ‘not boasting of goodness’ first among wishes—this too is the crux of conducting oneself!
translations.idiomatic: So Yan Hui ranked ‘no boasting of virtue’ above every wish—sound craft for any life.’

translations.literal: [53] Critical apparatus marker [53] stands here in the transmitted text.
translations.idiomatic: [53] The commentary apparatus inserts note fifty-three at this point.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：黃妖沖發，嵩乃奮鉞。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When the yellow demon burst forth Song raised the battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Yellow Chaos broke—Song lifted the axe.

sentences.zh: 孰是振旅，不居不伐。

translations.literal: Who then rallied the host yet claimed no dwelling and boasted no merit?
translations.idiomatic: Who recalled the columns yet seized no fief and claimed no praise?

sentences.zh: [54]儁㨗陳、穎，亦弭*

translations.literal: [54] Jun was swift in Chen and Ying,
translations.idiomatic: [54] Jun swept Chen and Ying,

translations.literal: (yú)
translations.idiomatic: (variant graph yú ‘at/in’)

translations.literal: **[and]** stilled the Yue frontier.
translations.idiomatic: and quieted the Yue marches.

sentences.zh: [55]言肅王命，並遘屯蹷。

translations.literal: [55] They voiced solemn royal commands yet alike stumbled into setbacks.
translations.idiomatic: [55] Both bore imperial mandate—and both tripped on fate.

translations.literal: [56] Editorial apparatus marker [56] closes the encomium.
translations.idiomatic: [56] The stanza ends with commentary tag fifty-six.

translations.idiomatic: Collation: the Ji woodblock uses a different character for Jun in the chapter title.

translations.idiomatic: A parallel text reads ‘wards’ where this one reads ‘cells.’

translations.idiomatic: Editions disagree on whether the river is spelled with one syllable-graph or another.

translations.idiomatic: Yuan texts record the nephew’s name with three different homophone spellings.

sentences.zh: 二三〇六頁 八行 專命雖罪專誅亦有責也 按：《集解》引王補說，謂《通鑒》作「違命雖罪」，故胡注卓不釋兵為違命，嵩勑討卓為專誅。

translations.idiomatic: Wang Bu notes the comprehensive mirror version stresses disobedience; Hu Sanxing explains how each man’s act maps to that language.

translations.idiomatic: Opening of sacrificial-meat gloss.

translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice versus campaign ritual meats.

translations.literal: Erya states: ‘When undertaking great affairs and moving great hosts one must first conduct business at the altar of soil before departing—this is called yi.’
translations.idiomatic: Erya defines the yi rite.

sentences.zh: 新序曰：「楚白公勝既殺令尹、司馬，欲立王子閭為王。

translations.literal: New Arrangements states: ‘Chu noble Gong Sheng Bai had already killed the chief minister and marshal and wished to enthrone Prince Min.
translations.idiomatic: Xinxu anecdote on Bai Gong begins.

sentences.zh: 王子閭不肯，劫之以刃。

translations.literal: Prince Min refused; Bai threatened him with blades.
translations.idiomatic: Coercion scene.

sentences.zh: 王子閭曰：『吾聞辭天下者，非輕其利以明其德也。

translations.literal: Prince Min said: ‘I have heard that those who decline All Under Heaven do not slight profit in order to display virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Min’s refusal speech opens.

sentences.zh: 不為諸侯者，非惡其位以絜其行也。

translations.literal: Those who reject becoming feudal lords do not hate position in order to polish conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Second parallel clause.

sentences.zh: 今子告我以利，威我以兵，吾不為也。

translations.literal: Now you notify me with profit and intimidate me with arms—I will not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Refusal to usurp.

sentences.zh: 』白公強之，不可，遂殺之。

translations.idiomatic: Murder for refusal.

translations.idiomatic: Restoration after coup.

translations.idiomatic: Gloss tying coalition to note.

translations.idiomatic: Shangshu citation on Yi Yin.

translations.literal: Analects states: ‘How can it compare to common men and women clutching petty good faith?
translations.idiomatic: Confucius on small fidelity.

sentences.zh: 」《莊子》云，孔子見盜跖，退曰：「吾幾不免虎口。」

translations.literal: ’ Zhuangzi states Confucius met Robber Zhi and withdrew saying: ‘I barely escaped the tiger’s jaws.’
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi tiger-jaws metaphor.

translations.idiomatic: Early office.

translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin style name.

sentences.zh: 斂策，不論其功。

translations.literal: Folding the stratagems means not debating his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Idiom gloss on modesty.

translations.literal: Analects states Yan Hui said: ‘I wish not to boast of goodness nor broadcast my labors.’
translations.idiomatic: Yan Hui’s humble vow.

translations.literal: Laozi states: ‘When merit is achieved do not dwell on it.’
translations.idiomatic: Dao de jing on non-attachment.
